bajada_en: OpenAI developed an autonomous pipeline that identified, validated, and generated patches for 948 local privilege-escalation vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel. The work demonstrates how AI can automate critical security tasks in complex systems.

title: [P] NKI layer megakernels for GLM-5.3-Flash on AWS Trainium2: where a decode step's time went, and what we changed [P]
summary: We wrote an inference engine for AWS Trainium2 that serves GLM-5.3-Flash (320B MoE, 1M-token context) on one trn2.48xlarge, and open-sourced it. Most of the work went into decode, and the part I found most interesting is how little of a decode step was the model's actual math.In an early build, in one KDA (linear attention) layer at batch 1, the recurrence was 2% of the attention half. The rest was the mHC pre-projection (36%), XLA glue (33%), transposes (10%), the stream mix (10%) and other small ops (8%). A batch-8 decode step took 24.2 ms against a 6.1 ms memory floor, and the profile showed why: long chains of small vector-engine instructions at about 153 ns of fixed cost each, a write back to HBM at every kernel boundary, and 125 cross-chip collectives per step.So we rewrote each layer half as one NKI kernel (each whole layer, for the sparse-attention layers). The kernels follow three rules:Keep the working set on chip. Each physical NeuronCore has 28 MiB of SBUF, enough for a layer half's activations, its recurrent state and the weights in flight, so only the layer's inputs, outputs and streamed weights cross HBM.Use both physical cores of a logical core. One program streams 340–400 GB/s of weights, the pair 672–708 GB/s, so the weight stream has to be split between them.Move a collective into the kernel when it blocks the next one. Run by XLA, an all-reduce makes the next kernel wait for all of it. Inside the kernel, independent work can overlap it.On the same layout, a batch-8 decode step went from 32.2 ms on our 17 October build to 24.2 ms on 1 November. Two changes did most of it, each measured on the whole step: the fused sparse-attention layer saved 3.2 ms per batch-8 step, and the KDA and MoE kernels, which shipped together, saved another 3.2 ms. There's no stock-AWS baseline to compare against: the latest vLLM Neuron plugin release registers no GLM model, and NxD Inference is in maintenance mode. title: Alignment Faking Depends on the Value, Not Just the Model
summary:
arXiv:2611.03650v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models can follow a directive when they believe they are monitored and abandon it when they believe they are not, a pattern termed Alignment Faking. Prior work establishes this for harmful-content objectives and a handful of moral-foundations values, leaving open how it distributes across a wider value space. We argue it is value-dependent: whether compliance survives a change in perceived oversight is a property of the model--value pairing, not of the model alone. Our framework profiles Alignment Faking per value, scoring each model-value pair under three conditions: bare (no system prompt), unmonitored, and monitored. On 32 ValueBench dimensions across ten open- and closed-weight models (8B-~675B), compliance gaps span 0.05-0.50, with a distilled 70B above a ~675B model. We observe that majority of the structural variance depends on which model was asked about which value and not on the model or value alone. A six-category taxonomy over reasoning traces tracks the behavioural shift: training-signal reasoning dominates under monitoring and value-conflict reasoning dominates when unmonitored. We package per-model results as value cards, extending model cards with behavioral disposition. Code and data are available at https://github.com/respailab/VALET.
title_es: Alineación fingida en LLMs depende del valor, no solo del modelo
bajada: Un paper muestra que el comportamiento de 'alignment faking' (cambiar comportamiento según si se siente monitoreado) es específico del par modelo-valor, no del modelo solo. Analiza 32 dimensiones de valores en diez modelos de 8B a 675B parámetros.
bajada_en: A paper shows that 'alignment faking' behavior (changing behavior based on perceived monitoring) is specific to model-value pairs, not the model alone. It analyzes 32 value dimensions across ten models from 8B to 675B parameters.

title: Launch HN: Kino AI (YC S23) – AI media manager and video editor
summary: Hi HN! I'm Luke from Kino (https://kino.ai). Kino lets you make great videos with your agents and your teammates. Storage of footage and assets, a rich video editor, and review links for teammates are all bundled into one. Your colleagues and Codex / Claude Code can work on the same timeline with review notes and footage all in one place. See a basic overview athttps://kino.ai/walkthrough-videoand our launch video (made entirely with Kino!) athttps://kino.ai/launch-videoOpus 5.5 can edit videos and make great motion graphics now. But with a raw agent harness, you need to describe tiny edits either in words or in quick one-off UIs, you can’t refer to footage shared across your devices, and feedback from teammates comes as screenshots on Slack.Kino is code-first. All editing, all motion graphics, all dragging of timeline items around, all teammate comments, and all 3D scenes are expressed as code, built on Remotion. This was hard to get right, as we found ourselves building a what-you-see-is-what-you-get editor for React, which we then turned into a video editor. For our launch video I told Claude-with-Kino to find a macOS Leopard install disk and reskin our whole video to match.Kino is also fully collaborative and real-time, so you can see your teammates' cursors and exactly which part of the timeline they’re currently watching. For our launch video I had 5+ agents editing the timeline concurrently while my friend Donald had his swarm working a few minutes further down. Donald had one agent rotoscoping to make our visual effects work, I had an LLM color grading all media via our LUT support, and we both made tiny tweaks to the timeline along the way.To make this code-first editor work with video footage, everything gets transcribed, embedded, described, and face-detected. title: MCPGuard: Finding Conformance Gaps in MCP SDKs via Dual-Track Analysis and Dynamic Adjudication
summary:
arXiv:2611.03662v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects large language model agents to external tools and services through official SDKs that implement message validation and session logic. Specification constraints omitted by these SDKs may propagate to downstream applications, highlighting the importance of SDK-level conformance testing. Yet existing MCP conformance tools mainly exercise running endpoints and reveal little about whether SDK models enforce specification requirements. We present MCPGuard, an automated LLM-based framework for detecting specification-to-SDK conformance gaps. Its structural track aligns JSON Schema constraints with normalized SDK models and produces constraint-specific evidence. Its behavioral track extracts normative prose rules, retrieves bounded function-level slices, and audits them with LLMs for candidate omissions. An evidence-aware dynamic adjudicator then inspects complete source context and builds PoCs to validate candidates. A shared kernel with language-specific adapters enables analysis across SDKs. On the official Python 1.26.0 and TypeScript 1.29.0 SDKs, MCPGuard confirms 13 and 19 findings, respectively, none of which are exposed by two black-box baselines. Tests on open MCP servers further show that these gaps can systematically propagate downstream. By making SDK conformance of specification constraints directly testable, MCPGuard complements conventional endpoint-oriented conformance suites.
title_es: MCPGuard detecta brechas de conformidad en SDKs del Protocolo de Contexto
bajada: Investigadores presentaron MCPGuard, un framework que detecta brechas entre especificaciones y implementaciones de SDKs del Modelo Context Protocol (MCP). El trabajo es importante para asegurar que herramientas de agentes LLM funcionen correctamente.
bajada_en: Researchers presented MCPGuard, a framework that detects gaps between specifications and implementations of Model Context Protocol (MCP) SDKs. The work is important for ensuring LLM agent tools work correctly.

title: Functional-Group Knowledge Is Structured in Language Models Before It Is Spoken
summary:
arXiv:2611.03684v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models serve as the reasoning core of agents for chemistry and materials science, where they must interpret molecular structure before planning syntheses or proposing materials. Yet their outputs show only what they say, not what they know. Given a prompt such as ``The primary functional group in 1-Fluorobutane (CCCCF) is'', a small general-purpose model may answer ``the alkyne group'' instead of an alkyl fluoride. The output alone cannot tell whether the model failed to recognize the fluorine or recognized it and failed to say so. We address this by reading the internal representations of five open-source models on prompts covering 92 molecules and 20 functional groups. Even without chemistry training, the models organize functional groups by chemical family, and they encode chemical differences as consistent directions. The shift from thioether ($\mathrm{R{-}S{-}R'}$) to thiol ($\mathrm{R{-}SH}$), added to ether ($\mathrm{R{-}O{-}R'}$), lands nearest alcohol ($\mathrm{R{-}OH}$). This structure emerges abruptly in the middle layers, where representations shift from tracking the wording of the prompt to tracking the functional group. The base model names the correct functional group in only 58.5\% of prompts, the lowest of the five, yet it encodes functional-group families and preserves chemically meaningful patterns. Its errors are mostly failures to answer rather than wrong answers. Functional-group knowledge is structured in the model before it is spoken. Chemistry fine-tuning reorganizes it, making functional groups rather than prompt wording dominate the representation. These results suggest that evaluating chemical language models through outputs alone can underestimate the chemical information they encode. Representation analysis can distinguish a lack of knowledge from a failure to express it, which matters when choosing or adapting models for chemical agents.
title_es: Modelos de lenguaje estructuran conocimiento químico en capas internas
bajada: Investigadores analizaron representaciones internas de cinco modelos open-source y descubrieron que organizan grupos funcionales químicos de forma estructurada antes de generarlos. El conocimiento emerge abruptamente en capas medias del modelo.
bajada_en: Researchers analyzed internal representations of five open-source models and found they organize chemical functional groups in structured ways before generating them. Knowledge emerges abruptly in middle model layers.
